records.label: III:2 (proband)
records.family: Chinese family with two infertile brothers
records.segregation: Father heterozygous for c.2071C>G, mother heterozygous for c.529+5G>A; affected brother is also compound heterozygous
quotes: The proband (III:2) was a 30-year-old Chinese man.
Semen centrifugal sediment smear showed that the sperm count was 0–1 cells per high-power field (HPF) revealing cryptozoospermia.

A novel compound heterozygous mutation was identified in the meiotic double-stranded break formation protein 1 (MEI1) gene (Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man [OMIM]: 608797), including the missense mutation c.2071C>G (p.Gln691Glu) located in exon 18 and the splicing mutation c.529+5G>A located downstream of exon 5.

records.label: III:3 (brother)
records.family: Chinese family with two infertile brothers
records.segregation: Inherited one variant from each heterozygous parent
quotes: Several semen tests indicated that no sperm could be found in his initial semen smear, but 0–1 motile sperm were occasionally seen after the semen centrifugation smear, also revealing cryptozoospermia.

This compound heterozygous mutation was confirmed by Sanger sequencing in the proband and his brother. The father (II:2) of the brothers was a c.2071C>G heterozygous carrier, while their mother (II:3) was a c.529+5G>A heterozygous carrier (Figure 1).

records.label: Four Chinese patients with NOA
quotes: bi-allelic deleterious variants in meiosis inhibitor protein 1 (MEI1) were identified by whole-exome sequencing in four Chinese patients with NOA

Testicular pathologic analysis and immunohistochemical staining revealed that spermatogenesis is arrested at spermatocyte stage, with defective programmed DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) homoeostasis and meiotic chromosome synapsis in patients carrying the variants.

quotes: a female infertile patient with embryonic arrest from one consanguineous family
Highly chromosomal anomalies were revealed in arrested embryos with MEI1 mutation.

notes.statement: Liu et al. (2025) found that the homozygous MEI1 exon 19 deletion was confirmed by cDNA sequencing, resulted in almost no detectable expression of exon 19 in patients, and on Western blot of transfected HEK293T cells produced a truncated MEI1 protein consistent with premature termination at exon 20.
quotes: Amplification and sequencing of the cDNA verified the deletion of whole exon of MEI1.
Quantitative expression revealed that the deletion result in almost no detectable expression of MEI1 Exon 19 in patients
Western blotting revealed that the whole exon deletion in MEI1 result in production of truncated MEI1 protein, corresponding to the predicted premature termination at Exon 20 of MEI1.

notes.statement: Liu et al. (2025) found high rates of chromosomal anomalies on preimplantation genetic testing of arrested embryos with MEI1 mutation and suggested that embryonic aneuploidy may underlie decreased developmental potential and embryonic arrest.
quotes: Highly chromosomal anomalies were revealed in arrested embryos with MEI1 mutation.
also revealed the aneuploidies of embryos with MEI1 mutation as a potential reason for declined developmental potency and embryonic arrest

notes.statement: Zhang et al. (2023) found that the MEI1 missense variant c.G186C reduced MEI1 expression and the frameshift variant c.251delT produced truncated MEI1 protein in vitro. Based on bioinformatic analysis, they suggested that the missense variant c.T1585A affected the interaction between MEI1 and its partners.
quotes: one missense variant (c.G186C) reduced the expression of MEI1 and one frameshift variant (c.251delT) led to truncated proteins of MEI1 in in vitro
the missense variant (c.T1585A) was assumed to affect the interaction between MEI1 and its partners via bioinformatic analysis

notes.statement: In testicular tissue from patients with bi-allelic MEI1 variants, Zhang et al. (2023) found defective homeostasis of programmed DNA double-strand breaks and defective meiotic chromosome synapsis. They concluded that these defects lead to meiotic arrest and male infertility.
quotes: bi-allelic variants in MEI1 could cause defective DSBs homoeostasis and meiotic chromosome synapsis, which subsequently lead to meiosis arrest and male infertility

notes.statement: Chen et al. (2023) noted that the MEI1 variants in the two affected brothers were inherited from their parents, each a single heterozygous carrier, which indicated a recessive pattern of inheritance.
quotes: The mutations were inherited from their parents, who were both single heterozygous carriers, indicating a recessive pattern of inheritance.

notes.statement: Chen et al. (2023) suggested that together, the two compound heterozygous MEI1 variants (a splice variant and a missense variant) may allow slight MEI1 expression. This could sometimes allow meiosis to proceed, which would explain why the brothers had cryptozoospermia rather than the nonobstructive azoospermia seen with other MEI1 variants.
quotes: We can suggest that the combination of the two heterozygous variants may cause slight expression of MEI1 and thus sometimes allow meiosis to occur, resulting in cryptozoospermia rather than NOA.

notes.statement: Chen et al. (2023) reported that varSEAK predicted the c.529+5G>A variant as class 5, likely to affect splicing, and that several prediction programs predicted the c.2071C>G missense variant to be deleterious. Neither variant was present in ExAC or gnomAD. No functional studies were possible because too few sperm were available and no testicular tissue was obtained.
quotes: The splicing mutation of c.529+5G>A is predicted to be class 5 according to the splice site variation prediction website varSEAK (https://varseak.bio/index.php), which likely will affect gene splicing.
These two variants have not been included in ExAC or gnomAD thus far.

Due to the extremely limited availability of sperm from the brothers, the MEI1 mRNA or MEI1 protein in sperm cannot be evaluated, and their testicular tissue cannot be obtained for further immunohistochemistry studies.

notes.statement: Malcher et al. (2022) performed whole-genome sequencing on 39 men with nonobstructive azoospermia (NOA) and identified candidate NOA-associated variants in 29 of them. These included variants in genes not previously linked to NOA (TKTL1, IGSF1, ZFPM2, VCX3A) and in genes already known to be associated with infertility. In 5 of 6 patients with earlier nondiagnostic whole-exome sequencing, WGS found variants in NOA-associated genes.
quotes: In this study, we identified novel potential candidate NOA-associated genes in 29 individuals out of 39 azoospermic males. Note that in 5 out of 6 patients subjected previously to WES analysis, which did not disclose potentially causative variants, the WGS analysis was successful with NOA-associated gene findings.

notes.statement: In the cohort studied by Malcher et al. (2022), testicular histology showed postmeiotic arrest in 16 patients, meiotic arrest in 3, premeiotic arrest in 3, and Sertoli-cell-only syndrome in 10. All patients had a normal karyotype, no Y chromosome microdeletions and no CFTR mutations.
quotes: postmeiotic arrest (Johnsen score 6–9: 16 samples), meiotic arrest (Johnsen score 4–5: 3 samples), premeiotic arrest (Johnsen score 3: 3 samples), and Sertoli‐cell‐only syndrome (SCOS; Johnsen score 2: 10 samples)
All the patients were tested and did not show the following causes of infertility: abnormal karyotype, Y chromosome microdeletions, CFTR gene mutations

notes.statement: Malcher et al. (2022) found that both patients with TKTL1 variants had no TKTL1 expression at the mRNA or protein level. Structural modeling predicted that the frameshift truncates most of the protein and that E534G destabilizes the C-terminal domain, which helps mediate homodimerization.
quotes: For both patients, we observed lack of expression of the TKTL1 gene at both mRNA and protein levels (Figure S2C,D).

homodimerization is in part mediated by the C‐terminal domain, suggesting that a mutation that destabilizes the fold of this domain could destabilize the quaternary structure of the functional protein

notes.statement: Nguyen et al. (2018) identified biallelic deleterious mutations in MEI1, TOP6BL/C11orf80, and REC114, genes with roles in the formation of meiotic double-strand breaks, in women with recurrent androgenetic complete hydatidiform moles.
quotes: We identified bi-allelic deleterious mutations in MEI1, TOP6BL/C11orf80, and REC114, with roles in meiotic double-strand breaks formation in women with recurrent androgenetic complete hydatidiform moles.

notes.statement: Nguyen et al. (2018) found that in Mei1-deficient female mice, 8% of oocytes lost all their chromosomes by extruding them with the spindles into the first polar body. Mei1-/- oocytes could be fertilized, and 5% produced androgenetic zygotes.
quotes: We investigated the occurrence of androgenesis in Mei1-deficient female mice and discovered that 8% of their oocytes lose all their chromosomes by extruding them with the spindles into the first polar body.
We demonstrate that Mei1-/- oocytes are capable of fertilization and 5% produce androgenetic zygotes.
